 from __future__ import annotations
@@ -2351,6 +2353,106 @@ def _record_append_recovery(
     _atomic_private_write(path, payload)
 
 
+def _validate_reconstructed_append(
+    completed: bytes,
+    journal: Mapping[str, Any],
+) -> None:
+    """Authenticate the intended operation and its reconstructed ledger state."""
+
+    payload = str(journal["payload"]).encode("utf-8")
+    try:
+        intended = json.loads(payload)
+    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
+        raise CalibrationLedgerError(
+            "append recovery refused: intended operation is malformed"
+        ) from exc
+    receipts, chain_reasons = _parse_ledger(completed)
+    if (
+        chain_reasons
+        or not receipts
+        or not _valid_receipt_shape(intended)
+        or receipts[-1] != intended
+        or int(intended["sequence"]) != len(receipts)
+        or intended["predecessor_digest"] != journal["predecessor_digest"]
+    ):
+        raise CalibrationLedgerError(
+            "append recovery refused: reconstructed ledger chain is invalid"
+        )
+
+    observations, sessions, state_reasons = _attempts_and_observations(receipts)
+    event = str(intended["event"])
+    expected_state_reasons: set[str] = set()
+    if event in {"reservation", HISTORICAL_IMPORT_RESERVATION_EVENT}:
+        expected_state_reasons.add("calibration_ledger_pending")
+    elif intended.get("schema_version") == BRACKET_SESSION_SCHEMA and (
+        event
+        in {
+            BRACKET_SESSION_OPEN_EVENT,
+            BRACKET_SESSION_SLOT_CLAIM_EVENT,
+        }
+        or event == BRACKET_SESSION_FINALIZATION_EVENT
+        and intended.get("slot") == "pre"
+    ):
+        expected_state_reasons.add("calibration_ledger_bracket_session_open")
+    if state_reasons != expected_state_reasons:
+        raise CalibrationLedgerError(
+            "append recovery refused: expected operation or session identity is invalid"
+        )
+
+    if intended.get("schema_version") == BRACKET_SESSION_SCHEMA:
+        session = next(
+            (
+                item
+                for item in sessions
+                if item.session_id == intended.get("session_id")
+            ),
+            None,
+        )
+        if session is None or any(
+            getattr(session, field) != intended.get(field)
+            for field in (
+                "session_id",
+                "window_id",
+                "plan_id",
+                "plan_sha256",
+                "evidence_root_id",
+                "runs_root",
+            )
+        ):
+            raise CalibrationLedgerError(
+                "append recovery refused: expected operation or session identity is invalid"
+            )
+        operation_matches = {
+            BRACKET_SESSION_OPEN_EVENT: (
+                session.capability_receipt_digest == intended["receipt_digest"]
+            ),
+            BRACKET_SESSION_SLOT_CLAIM_EVENT: session.state == "open",
+            BRACKET_SESSION_FINALIZATION_EVENT: (
+                intended.get("slot") in session.finalized_slots
+                and session.finalized_slots[str(intended["slot"])].receipt_digest
+                == intended["receipt_digest"]
+            ),
+            BRACKET_SESSION_ABORT_EVENT: (
+                session.abort_receipt_digest == intended["receipt_digest"]
+            ),
+        }.get(event, False)
+    else:
+        matching_observations = [
+            observation
+            for observation in observations
+            if observation.attempt_id == intended.get("attempt_id")
+            and observation.receipt_digest == intended["receipt_digest"]
+        ]
+        operation_matches = (
+            event in {"reservation", HISTORICAL_IMPORT_RESERVATION_EVENT}
+            or len(matching_observations) == 1
+        )
+    if not operation_matches:
+        raise CalibrationLedgerError(
+            "append recovery refused: expected operation or session identity is invalid"
+        )
+
+
 def _clear_append_journal(ledger_path: Path) -> None:
     try:
         _append_journal_path(ledger_path).unlink()

The pinned closure was: refuse zero-byte intents without replay; validate the reconstructed operation, session identity and ledger state before clearing the journal; add never-started-abort and copied-foreign-journal regressions.
CHARGE:

(2) Did it BREAK the legitimate paths? Re-run the original torn-tail and complete-tail recovery scenarios and confirm they still heal exactly as before.
(3) Are the two new regressions discriminating? Mutate the new guard (remove the zero-byte check; then separately remove the identity validation) and confirm a test fails in each case; revert.
(4) Introduced defects: does refusing zero-byte intents create a state an operator cannot exit — i.e. a journal that can now never be cleared by any governed path? Walk that explicitly; a custody artifact that fails closed into an unexitable state is its own strand-a-night.
(5) Same-signature: does the auto-replay/foreign-journal class survive in any form — yes/no.
Report the focused ledger suite tail. CLEAN needs a checks-performed line.

<!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. de665ea"><span class="source-file">TASK_QUEUE.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit de665ea</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. de665ea"><span class="source-file">TASK_QUEUE.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit de665ea</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. de665ea"><span class="source-file">TASK_QUEUE.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit de665ea</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. Dated completion and disposition history remains below; the generated Current Queue region is the sole live work-selection view.</p> <h2 id="completed-queue-items">Completed Queue Items</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Priority</th> <th>Completed</th> <th>Task</th> <th>Evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>CODEX-BRIDGE-PET</td> <td>P4 Polish</td> <td>2026-07-18</td> <td>Make the native Codex pet reflect Claude Code background Sol work without changing adaptive effort routing</td> <td>No phase exit-checklist row exists for this personal bridge UI integration; de665ea"><span class="source-file">TASK_QUEUE.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit de665ea</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. de665ea"><span class="source-file">TASK_QUEUE.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit de665ea</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. de665ea"><span class="source-file">TASK_QUEUE.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit de665ea</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. ## Current Project Status

mainline.**

### The central measurement fact (read before any measurement decision)

The instrument is **attribution-limited (~1 J), not noise-limited
(~0.3 J)** — D-078 clause 11, Ed-ratified. Floors publish LABELLED with
the widened number; the point floor is a repeatability diagnostic that
may never be the published claim floor. The anchor term appears in
**both** the floor and each claim's decision interval, so the effective
clearable effect is floor + claim-side bound ≈ 5 J for phase contrasts,
and neither term may later be deleted as an apparent double count. Do
not launch an instrument-tightening program; it was measured and
eliminated.
